title: Cooking a turkey Thursday? A 12- to 16-pound bird needs three to four days to thaw
excerpt: A refrigerator at 40°F or colder gives a turkey time to thaw safely. USDA’s Thanksgiving Day hotline opens at 7 a.m. Central.
locality: Pontotoc County households preparing Thanksgiving meals. The hotline serves callers nationwide.

paragraphs.text: If you’re cooking a 12- to 16-pound frozen turkey on Thanksgiving, Sunday is the time to clear a spot in the refrigerator. A bird in that weight range needs about three to four days to thaw, according to University of Georgia Cooperative Extension. Thanksgiving falls on Thursday, Nov. 26.

Leave the turkey in a container to catch drips and keep the refrigerator at 40°F or colder. A 16- to 20-pound bird can take four to five days. Once it has thawed in the refrigerator, you can keep it there another one to two days before cooking.

For a faster thaw, seal the turkey in a leakproof bag and submerge it in cold water. Allow about 30 minutes per pound and change the water every half hour. A 12-pound turkey takes about six hours this way and needs to go straight into the oven when thawed. Thawing on the kitchen counter is unsafe.

Before serving, use a thermometer in the thickest part of the breast and the innermost parts of the thigh and wing. Each should reach at least 165°F. If the turkey is stuffed, check the center of the stuffing for the same temperature.

For questions before the holiday, Mississippi State Extension lists its Pontotoc County office at 662-489-3910. On Thanksgiving Day, the USDA Meat and Poultry Hotline will take calls at 888-674-6854 from 7 a.m. to 1 p.m. Central.
